description: Game web development and space Exploration
summary: Abandoned but Not Forgotten” is a storytelling project—featured in the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge—that documents the hardware NASA has left behind since the 1960s on the Moon, Mars, and across deep space, from Apollo landers and lunar rovers to retired Martian robots like Spirit, Opportunity, and Ingenuity. Built from NASA archives and open mission data, it transforms dense technical records into engaging narratives detailing each object’s history, scientific purpose, and present status, brought to life through interactive maps, timelines, animations, graphic novels, and audio stories. The project matters because it preserves off-world human heritage, raises awareness of space debris and site protection as lunar and Martian activity grows, and bridges public disconnection by making complex science emotional and accessible. Ultimately, it inspires young learners and school-age enthusiasts while reminding everyone that these silent machines still carry lasting meaning.
details: Abandoned but not Forgotten is an interactive digital space-heritage platform that transforms dormant NASA equipment on the Moon and Mars—such as Apollo landers, rovers, and parachutes—into engaging, first-person micro-stories. Built on standard laptops using Python, HTML5/CSS3/JavaScript, PowerPoint/Google Slides, Canva, and Synthetic Intelligence (SI) tools, it curates verified mission logs and imagery from official NASA archives (PDS, LRO, HiRISE) and publishes them via open, registration-free links. By giving silent spacecraft a personal voice and pairing them with a 30-second animated clip, the project makes STEM learning accessible, builds a zero-cost virtual museum, and reframes discarded hardware from "space junk" into historic monuments. Throughout development, our team prioritized strict scientific accuracy, open accessibility without logins, scalability for upcoming Artemis missions, and ethical transparency—including visible SI-generated watermarks and explicit disclosures for SI audio and NASA data.
